raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
In 256-GPU torchtitan + torchft chaos runs with the native nccl2 process group (finding 11 in the report), one local rank per host blocked for 60 s in the reconfigure commRevoke after a shrink. Its peers were already in FSDP collectives that need that rank, and the intra-replica watchdog (`comm.train_timeout_seconds=60`) fired at the same moment the reconfigure timed out (torchft manager timeout, hard-coded default 60 s). The watchdog won on 11 of 29 hosts and SIGABRTed every rank, including rank 0, which hosts the ManagerServer. That turned a recoverable reconfigure failure into replica teardowns (56 aborts in one burst).

Fix: add `fault_tolerance.timeout_ms` (default 60000, unchanged behavior), pass it to `torchft.Manager`, and log a warning when the effective timeout (`TORCHFT_TIMEOUT_SEC` overrides it) is not below `comm.train_timeout_seconds`. The docstring notes that it also bounds checkpoint transfer during recovery.

Test plan:
- `pytest torchtitan/experiments/torchft/tests/test_torchft_manager.py` (new `test_timeout_is_passed_to_manager`)
- pre-commit (pyrefly not installed locally)

This PR was authored with AI assistance.

detail.title: [torchft] Make the torchft manager timeout configurable

files.patch:
@@ -59,6 +59,16 @@ class Config(Configurable.Config):
         Note: This currently only works with gloo process group.
         """
 
+        timeout_ms: int = 60000
+        """
+        Timeout for torchft manager operations, including process group
+        reconfiguration. Keep it below comm.train_timeout_seconds: a rank blocked
+        in reconfiguration stops issuing its intra-replica collectives, so its
+        peers' watchdog aborts the replica if this timeout is longer. It also
+        bounds checkpoint transfer during recovery, so leave room for that.
+        TORCHFT_TIMEOUT_SEC overrides it.
+        """
+
         replica_id: int = 0
         """The TorchFT replica ID of this run."""
 
@@ -133,6 +143,7 @@ def __init__(
             state_dict=None,
             use_async_quorum=config.use_async_quorum and self.use_async_quorum,
             replica_id=f"torchtitan_ft_{config.replica_id}",
+            timeout=timedelta(milliseconds=config.timeout_ms),
         )
         self.group_size = config.group_size
         self.replica_id = config.replica_id

@@ -10,6 +10,7 @@
 torchft surface used by the manager is replaced with recording doubles.
 """
 
+from datetime import timedelta
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 from unittest import mock
 
@@ -78,3 +79,9 @@ def test_semi_sync_training_always_uses_synchronous_quorum(
     assert ft_manager.use_async_quorum is False
     assert not hasattr(ft_manager, "replicate_pg")
     assert ft_manager.loss_sync_pg is None
+
+
+def test_timeout_is_passed_to_manager(torchft_doubles):
+    build_manager(timeout_ms=30000)
+
+    assert torchft_doubles.Manager.call_args.kwargs["timeout"] == timedelta(seconds=30)

@@ -85,6 +85,15 @@ def _initialize_distributed_runtime(self) -> None:
             pipeline_parallel_degree=config.parallelism.pipeline_parallel_degree,
         )
         self.ft_manager = self.fault_tolerance.build()
+        if self.fault_tolerance.enable:
+            # TORCHFT_TIMEOUT_SEC overrides fault_tolerance.timeout_ms.
+            ft_timeout = self.ft_manager.manager._timeout.total_seconds()
+            if ft_timeout >= config.comm.train_timeout_seconds:
+                logger.warning(
+                    f"torchft manager timeout ({ft_timeout} s) should be below "
+                    f"comm.train_timeout_seconds ({config.comm.train_timeout_seconds}); "
+                    "a slow process group reconfiguration can otherwise abort the replica."
+                )
         self.parallelism_context = ParallelismContext.from_config(
